## Critique
- claim-1: The basiswise proof is correct. Transposition bijects partitions in \(q^r\) containing \(i^j\) with partitions in \(r^q\) containing \(j^i\), including \(i=0\), \(j=0\), and consequently \(r=0\) or \(q=0\). Thus the Schur bases are mapped bijectively and the asserted interval-ideal equality follows. The ideal argument is also valid by Littlewood–Richardson containment. Relative to the standard Schur involution, the named certificate is established without asserting the parent theorem.
